chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Bureyd al-Ijli, who said:

Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) was asked about a man against whom witnesses testified that he had broken his fast during the month of Ramadan for three days. He (peace be upon him) said: 'He is asked,

He is asked, "Is there a sin upon you regarding your breaking the fast during the month of Ramadan?" So if he says, "No", then it is upon the Imam to kill him; and if he says, "Yes", then it is upon the Imam to flog him.

key_terms.يَنْهَكَهُ: He flogs him / He strikes him

ai.seo_question: What is the difference in punishment for breaking fast if one denies the sin versus admitting it?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi details the judicial mechanism of *ikhrāj* (eliciting confession) used by the Imam to determine the penalty for deliberate fasting violation. It distinguishes between *qatl* (execution) for those who deny the sin, implying a higher degree of culpability or *hudud* severity, and *nahk* (corporal punishment) for those who admit, reflecting the Shia jurisprudential nuance between fixed punishments and discretionary penalties.
